author: NorthEast News Desk
body: A free downtown Boston block party brought salsa music and cultural programming to Summer Street Plaza on Saturday. The Embrace Massó “¡Con Salsa!” event ran from 3 to 7 p.m. in Downtown Crossing, with Puerto Rican salsa orchestra El Gran Combo de Puerto Rico serving as the headline act.

Organized by Embrace Boston, the gathering was designed to celebrate the links among Black culture, Latino identity and the wider African diaspora. The program combined live music, dancing and public art in a central pedestrian area, turning a city block into an open-air community venue.

The event also came as Embrace Boston expands its presence near Boston Common. The organization recently acquired 33 West Street, a building close to “The Embrace” memorial, as a future base for its civic and cultural work. Saturday’s party offered a public-facing version of that mission: using music and shared space to bring together communities whose histories in Boston overlap but are not always presented together. Admission was open to the public.
dek: El Gran Combo de Puerto Rico headlined the free Embrace Massó “¡Con Salsa!” gathering at Summer Street Plaza.
headline: Boston block party celebrates Black and Latino culture downtown
